subject: History
description: Mughal Emperor Jahangir (1605-1627) — life, marriage to Nur Jahan, Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, golden chain of justice, art and architecture.

questions.stem: Mughal Emperor JAHANGIR ascended to the throne in which year?
questions.explanation: JAHANGIR (born 1569 as Salim) — became Mughal Emperor in 1605 after AKBAR's death. Original name: NUR-UD-DIN MUHAMMAD SALIM; took regnal title JAHANGIR ('seizer of the world'). REIGN: 1605-1627 (22 years). MUGHAL EMPEROR SEQUENCE — memorize: (1) BABUR (1526-1530, founded Mughal empire after Battle of Panipat). (2) HUMAYUN (1530-1540, exiled by Sher Shah; restored 1555-1556). (3) AKBAR (1556-1605, the Great). (4) JAHANGIR (1605-1627). (5) SHAH JAHAN (1627-1658, built Taj Mahal). (6) AURANGZEB (1658-1707, expanded empire to peak). After Aurangzeb: rapid decline — Bahadur Shah I, Jahandar Shah, Farrukhsiyar, Muhammad Shah, etc. Last Mughal: BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR (deposed 1858 after 1857 Revolt). KEY EVENTS in JAHANGIR'S REIGN: (1) Marriage to NUR JAHAN (1611) — became co-ruler in practice. (2) GOLDEN CHAIN OF JUSTICE (Zanjir-i-Adl) outside Agra Fort — anyone could pull it to seek redress. (3) Captain Hawkins (1608) and Sir Thomas Roe (1615) — British East India Co. envoys at his court. (4) Annexation of Mewar (1614, Maharana Amar Singh I submitted). (5) Loss of KANDAHAR to Persia (1622). (6) GUSHED rebellion of son SHAH JAHAN (1623-26). PYQ FREQUENCY: Mughal chronology in SSC, UPSC, MPSC — 1-2 per cycle.

questions.explanation: TUZUK-I-JAHANGIRI (also JAHANGIRNAMA) — autobiographical memoirs of Emperor Jahangir, written by him in PERSIAN (with Turkish/Hindi blends). COVERAGE: from 1605 to 1622 (he stopped writing as health declined; SECRETARIES continued for last 5 years). CONTENT: keen observations on NATURE, ART, ARCHITECTURE, PEOPLE, animals, religious matters, court politics. Famous for DETAILED ANIMAL/PLANT descriptions (showing scientific curiosity rare for the era). PARALLEL TO BABURNAMA — Babur's memoirs (1483-1530) — also detailed nature observations; Jahangir clearly inherited the family literary tradition. KEY MUGHAL CHRONICLES (memorize): (1) BABURNAMA — Babur's memoirs (in Chagatai Turkic). (2) HUMAYUN-NAMA — by Gulbadan Begum (Humayun's sister), about Humayun. (3) AKBARNAMA — by ABUL FAZL, three volumes about Akbar. (4) AIN-I-AKBARI — third volume of Akbarnama, administrative gazetteer. (5) TUZUK-I-JAHANGIRI — by Jahangir himself. (6) PADSHAHNAMA — by ABDUL HAMID LAHORI, about Shah Jahan's reign. (7) ALAMGIRNAMA — by Mirza Muhammad Kazim, about Aurangzeb's first 10 years. (8) MUNTAKHAB-AT-TAWARIKH — by Badauni (critical/orthodox view of Akbar). PYQ FREQUENCY: Mughal source-author pairings in UPSC, MPSC, NCERT-driven SSC — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Jahangir's powerful queen and effective co-ruler was:
questions.explanation: NUR JAHAN (born MIHR-UN-NISA, 1577-1645) — Jahangir's 20th wife (married 1611), but his FAVOURITE and most influential. ORIGIN: of Persian descent; father MIRZA GHIYAS BEG (later titled ITIMAD-UD-DAULAH, finance minister). FIRST MARRIAGE: to Sher Afkan (a Mughal officer killed in 1607; some accounts allege Jahangir had him killed to claim her). RISE: from 1611 onwards, became 'PADSHAH BEGUM'; coins MINTED in HER NAME (rare for a queen). EFFECTIVELY CO-RULER: dictated court appointments, signed firmans (royal orders), held audiences. NUR JAHAN JUNTA: she + father (Itimad-ud-Daulah) + brother ASAF KHAN + Prince Khurram (Shah Jahan, married Asaf Khan's daughter Mumtaz). KEY MOMENTS: (1) 1620s — power struggle with PRINCE KHURRAM (Shah Jahan); supported a rival prince (Shahryar) for succession — but Khurram won after Jahangir's death (1627). (2) BUILT ITIMAD-UD-DAULAH'S TOMB (1622-28, Agra) — the 'BABY TAJ', precursor of Taj Mahal — finest pietra dura work. (3) Designed gardens — Nur Mahal Sarai (Punjab), Achabal Bagh (Kashmir). NIECE: MUMTAZ MAHAL (Asaf Khan's daughter), Shah Jahan's wife — Taj Mahal built for her. PYQ FREQUENCY: Nur Jahan in UPSC, SSC, NCERT modern — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Jahangir's famous 'CHAIN OF JUSTICE' (Zanjir-i-Adl) was installed at:
questions.explanation: ZANJIR-I-ADL (CHAIN OF JUSTICE) — golden chain installed by Jahangir at AGRA FORT, between the FORT WALL and a STONE COLUMN by the YAMUNA RIVER. Anyone with a grievance against an official could PULL THE CHAIN; bells would ring inside the fort, and the case would come directly to the Emperor for redressal. SYMBOLIC: showed Jahangir's commitment to JUSTICE accessible to all (in his words 'so that the oppressed cannot be denied justice'). 60 BELLS connected; chain length supposedly several feet. PRACTICAL USE: actually rang RARELY — most disputes went through normal courts. But the SYMBOL was powerful — captured imagination of poets, chroniclers, even European travellers (Sir Thomas Roe noted it in his memoirs, 1615-19). HISTORICAL: not the FIRST such chain — earlier Persian rulers (Anushirvan the Just, 6th c.) and Indian rulers (Vikramaditya legend) had similar institutions. AGRA FORT: built initially by AKBAR (1565-73), expanded by Jahangir + Shah Jahan. Made of RED SANDSTONE (Akbar) + WHITE MARBLE additions (Shah Jahan). KEY STRUCTURES inside: Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, Sheesh Mahal, Khas Mahal, Musamman Burj (where Shah Jahan was imprisoned by Aurangzeb). UNESCO HERITAGE 1983. PYQ FREQUENCY: Jahangir's chain in SSC, UPSC, MPSC — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which English ambassador was sent to Jahangir's court by King James I in 1615?

options.option_text: Sir Thomas Roe (East India Co. trade)

questions.explanation: SIR THOMAS ROE (~1581-1644) — official ambassador of King JAMES I of England to Jahangir's court (1615-1619). PURPOSE: secure trading rights for the BRITISH EAST INDIA COMPANY — particularly to set up factories at Surat and other ports. Earlier, CAPTAIN WILLIAM HAWKINS (1608-11) had been a UNOFFICIAL Mughal envoy — Jahangir gave him a Mughal officer rank but Hawkins was unable to secure formal trading concessions due to PORTUGUESE rivalry. ROE's ACHIEVEMENT: secured a 'Phirman' (royal decree) granting EIC the right to trade and establish a factory at SURAT (1615). KEY OBSERVATIONS in his journals: (1) Mughal court's wealth and ceremonial. (2) Jahangir's love of art, animals (zoo at court), wine. (3) Nur Jahan's quiet but vast power. (4) The competing influence of Portuguese Jesuits. SUBSEQUENT EUROPEANS at Mughal court: PORTUGUESE — first to arrive (Vasco da Gama 1498); maintained influence, supplied artists, missionaries. DUTCH — established VOC (Dutch East India Co.) factories. FRENCH — later, esp. under La Bourdonnais (1740s). LEGACY: Roe's mission INITIATED the SLOW BRITISH PENETRATION of India that culminated in colonial rule by 1757 (Plassey) onwards. PYQ FREQUENCY: Roe's mission in UPSC, SSC, NCERT — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Jahangir's father AKBAR named him SALIM after which Sufi saint who blessed his birth?
questions.explanation: SHEIKH SALIM CHISHTI (1478-1572) — Sufi saint of the CHISHTI ORDER. AKBAR was childless for years, lost previous infants. Sheikh Salim Chishti BLESSED him; soon after, prince SALIM (later Jahangir) was born in 1569 — named after the saint in gratitude. AKBAR was so moved that he MOVED HIS CAPITAL to FATEHPUR SIKRI (1571-85), where Sheikh Salim's tomb is located. The TOMB OF SHEIKH SALIM CHISHTI inside Fatehpur Sikri's mosque complex is a famous WHITE MARBLE pavilion with intricate JALI screens. Even today, women tie threads on the screens for blessings. CHISHTI ORDER: founded by KHWAJA MOINUDDIN CHISHTI (~1141-1236) at AJMER — DARGAH of MOINUDDIN draws ~10 lakh pilgrims annually for URS. Other key Chishti saints: NIZAMUDDIN AULIYA (Delhi, ~1238-1325) — disciple AMIR KHUSRAU was his close associate. BAKHTIYAR KAKI (Delhi, ~1173-1235). FARID-UD-DIN GANJSHAKAR (Pakpattan, ~1175-1265). FATEHPUR SIKRI: planned imperial city (1571-85), abandoned after Akbar's reign due to water scarcity; UNESCO World Heritage (1986). KEY STRUCTURES: Buland Darwaza, Diwan-i-Khas, Panch Mahal, Salim Chishti's tomb, Tomb of Akbar's son. PYQ FREQUENCY: Chishti-Akbar-Jahangir links in UPSC, SSC, MPSC — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Jahangir is particularly known as a great patron of which art form?
questions.explanation: JAHANGIR — generally considered the GREATEST PATRON of MUGHAL MINIATURE PAINTING. His personal interest, fine eye for detail, and discriminating commissioning produced the GOLDEN AGE of Mughal art (~1600-1620). KEY ARTISTS in his Atelier: (1) USTAD MANSUR — naturalist painter; depicted exotic birds, flowers, animals (Dodo, Zebra, Turkey, Tulips); titled 'NADIR-UL-ASR' (Wonder of the Age). (2) ABU AL-HASAN — court portraitist; titled 'NADIR-UZ-ZAMAN'. (3) BISHANDAS — portrait specialist. STYLE under Jahangir: shift from BATTLE/COURT SCENES (Akbar era) to more INTIMATE, NATURALISTIC, INDIVIDUAL portraits, animal/bird studies, allegorical subjects. INFLUENCE OF EUROPEAN ART: increased — Jahangir's collection had Albrecht Dürer prints and Italian paintings; cross-cultural fusion visible. PRESERVED IN: Victoria Memorial (Kolkata), Bharat Kala Bhavan (Varanasi), various royal libraries (Tehran, London). FAMOUS MASTERPIECES: 'Squirrels in a Plane Tree' (Mansur), 'Jahangir's Dream of King James I'. JAHANGIR himself is famously quoted: 'I can recognize the work of any of my painters in a single brush-stroke.' RELATED ARTS: he ALSO patronized JEWELLERY, CARPETS, METALWORK, but PAINTING was his clear passion. PYQ FREQUENCY: Mughal art-patron links in UPSC, NCERT, SSC GA 1× per cycle.
